steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Over here!
She sweeps a wall of mist behind you, a desperate barrier against the horde. Her hand finds yours, grip fierce and unyielding as she drags you toward a low wall.
For one fleeting second, the thunder of footsteps behind you stumbles. Then the pursuit resumes, a furious stampede that shakes the ground and promises no escape.

steps.speaker: Monster
steps.content: Roaaarrr—
[Red Flash]
The mist soon shreds apart. You hurl yourselves behind the wall just as razor-sharp claws rip through the space where you stood.
We can't keep this up. They're after me. I'll draw them off, and you—
Lichen presses a finger to her lips. Her other hand moves with practiced stealth, producing several paper figures from her sleeve.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Heaven and earth, lend me your striders... Go!

The words barely leave her lips when the paper figures twitch to life. These tiny, wobbling things tumble onto the ground and immediately begin burrowing. Within seconds, only a few small holes remain.
The rumbling beneath your feet stops. Then, impossibly, it shifts direction, rumbling away.
A tug at your sleeve. Lichen grins, gesturing for you to peek.
Over the wall, you watch the monsters circle in confusion before scattering, each chased by a little hopping paper figure that leads them farther and farther until they vanish.
Silence, at last. Safe in her shadow, you breathe in the sharp scent of blood and the bittersweet tang of medicinal elixirs. Your heart gradually settles, and your breathing slowly steadies.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: There. That little diversion trick should keep them busy for a while.
She turns, and for the first time in a while, the tension in her face melts away. Her hand rises, then settles gently on your head. This time, you don't pull away.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Fret not. They weren't sent for you. These little phantoms are all from my shifu, her way of disciplining a wayward disciple.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I committed the ultimate transgression, you see. Had the nerve to use some arcane tricks against her. She must be absolutely livid.
Her voice carries laughter, light and easy, but her lips barely move, frozen in that same faint smile she wore moments ago. The one she wore when she drove back her own "shifu" to protect you.

options: ...Did you hurt her badly just now?

steps.content: You look worried.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Oh, it's nothing, really! I've been tinkering with exotic arts and mystical trinkets since I was small. Every time I got caught, she'd chase me from the peak to the foothills. She's long accustomed to it. She knows when to stop.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Once her temper cools, all will be well. For now, your situation is more...
A faint sound from behind cuts her off. Lichen spins, hand tightening around the bell—muscles coiled, ready.
But it's only the wind, stirring the paper talismans left by the wall.
She watches, waiting. The thin mist thins further, revealing nothing. Only then does she lower her eyes, the tension slowly leaving her shoulders as she looks away.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...Your situation is more pressing. Once you're safely settled, young friend, I'll find her and make amends.
She pulls out a talisman paper and a small vial streaked with bloodstains. She tries to wipe it clean on her sleeve, but the marks linger. She offers it to you anyway, along with an apologetic smile.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Such a timid soul, and yet you stood in front of me... You're a good child. I'd hate to leave you here alone. If you wandered into the Void of Yin again and got frightened, I'd never forgive myself.
...In truth, your concern has always been for her.

But now, as she pours water, her sleeve slides back, just enough to reveal the dark crimson wounds blooming on her skin. For the first time, you lower your head like an obedient child and simply listen.
She notices your gaze. With a small, subtle motion, her sleeve falls, hiding away the wounds.
...I'm not that timid, actually. The Void of Yin isn't so frightening. Not everything there is hostile.
Before I met you, there was a copper coin. It would protect me.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...A copper coin?
You nod. Lichen is taken aback for a moment, then lowers her head.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: It hasn't crossed any line yet, so what's there to worry about...
What did you say?

Her words slip away, too quiet to reach you. You ask her to repeat them. Her head snaps up, gaze fixed on you. A long pause stretches between you. Then she smiles, warm and a little wondering, and says:

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Well, you're here now. That changes things.
Before you can press further, the paper talisman in her hand ignites and dissolves into the water. In the same motion, the cup is at your lips, warm and fragrant with herbal ash.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Here, drink. If that coin has chosen you, then count it as another ally by your side.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Alas, my methods have always been... sweeping. Grand gestures and bold strokes. Using arts you don't understand would only frighten you. That would never do.
Her shoulders sag. Her gaze drops, and something dark flickers across her face. Then it's gone. She looks up with a smile and speaks gently to comfort you.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I'll find my shifu. At worst, I'll take a thorough scolding. Now that she's ascended, her heart must be far more magnanimous. She won't be too hard on me.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: But first, let's get you out of this city and back to the camp. With you, me, and the coin together, we should be able to break through this spectral maze.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That way, you can rest easy.
...What about you then? You're still going to look for her?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Mm-hmm.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I began this search alone anyway. If I lose my way, I'll simply cast another divination. The path will reveal itself.
...But can she really find her shifu?

Your shifu is now a denizen of the Void of Yin, beyond our reach. Earlier, just asking about her nearly pulled me into the abyss. We barely made it back. And now, even this realm is more dangerous than before.
You're just one person...
...The copper coin warned me, many times. Don't speak with the dead. Maybe that's what you'd call the Dao of Heaven. If you break that rule... the consequences could be worse than we can imagine.
She hears you out. Not a flicker of hesitation crosses her face, and when she answers, her voice is steady.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Would that not be a gift? If speaking with spirits leads me to a new world, I would walk that path gladly.
Words fail you. You don't know what to say, but she doesn't seem to notice. Her voice lifts, growing brighter, more spirited.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: This "abyss" people speak of—these "demons and devils"—they are merely shadows cast by fear. The common folk keep their distance, but how many have truly looked beyond the dark?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: If everyone clung to rules like that old relic, trembling at every shadow, they might as well entomb themselves in a museum and be done with it.
The words spill faster, faster. Her eyes slide away, fixed on something distant. She's murmuring to herself now, gone again.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The Dao of Heaven has shifted. Life and death blur. Yin and Yang fall out of balance. What room is left for all these rules? We have witnessed enough disasters. It is time someone sought new fortune amid the chaos. After all, fortune often lies within misfortune.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I will seek it. I will use it... Since she is already here, since someone has already crossed the boundary between life and death, then...
She catches the tension in your face. Her words trail off, unfinished. A soft sigh escapes her, and she smiles, warm and understanding.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Ah. There I go again. You are already the timid sort, young friend, and here I am rambling.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: But there is nothing to fear. With your help, I am stronger, but I will manage on my own, as I always have. Who knows? Going solo might let me truly spread my wings.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: It would not be right to rely on a child, anyway. Go on back now. When you are older, I will take you on another adventure. It is settled.
She raises a hand, patting your back gently. You look up, and all you see is blood, dark crimson staining her shoulder.
If you leave her alone, there's no telling how far she'll push herself. And she won't listen to persuasion. So there's only one choice left—
She raises her hand and flicks you on the forehead.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Are you going to listen to me or not?
You're not the only one who angered your "shifu." She was chasing me before you stepped in. With the old lady this furious, you really think she'd just let me walk away?
If we're going to apologize, wouldn't it be more sincere if we both went together? And if her anger doesn't cool, do you really think these ghosts will just let me leave in peace?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hmm... You do have a point...
Her brow furrows slightly, as if mulling something over. You quickly press on.
Besides, even if I tried to leave this city, who knows how long that would take. What if I fall asleep on the way? Then I'd have to face your shifu alone.
This is the honest truth. With your current body and strength, you have no confidence that you could make it out of Maria City on your own.
But with you by my side, I wouldn't be afraid. Not even if I fell asleep again.
I trust you. You'd wake me up, just like you did the first time.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Mm... No, no, that will not do! I cannot let you walk into danger again. What if something goes wrong?
You think fast. You know exactly what she likes to hear, so you tell her.

options: But I have you, don't I?

steps.content: The arts you used just now were incredible. That copper coin is nothing compared to you. One swat from a monster and it'd fly off who knows where.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Young friend, you mean to say...
I can't feel at ease unless I'm with you. Sending me back, relying on that coin... none of it's reliable. Staying by your side is the only way I'd feel safe!
Your words work like a charm. She nods enthusiastically.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...Well reasoned. Well reasoned indeed! It has been ages since I met someone so perceptive. You truly have more spirit than those stuffy old pedants.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Then let us be off! I am truly delighted. After all, the divination foretold it: you, young friend, would be my greatest blessing on this journey.
